G2100.def:
εὐαρεστέω, -ῶ 
[in LXX chiefly for הָלַךְ hith., Genèse 5:22, 24, Psaumes 26:2 56:13, al., Sir.44:16 ;] 
to be well pleasing: τ. θεῷ (LXX, ll. with), Hébreux 11:5-6. Pass., to be well pleased: with dative, Hébreux 13:16.†

G2101.def:
εὐ-άρεστος, -ον 
[in LXX: Wis.4:10 9:10 * ;] 
well-pleasing, acceptable: Romains 12:2; with dative of person(s), Romains 12:1 14:16, 2 Corinthiens 5:9, Éphésiens 5:10, Philippiens 4:18; id. before ἐν, Tite 2:9 (κυρίῳ), Colossiens 3:20; ἐνώπιον, Hébreux 13:21 (for ex. in Inser., see Deiss., BS, 215).†

G2102.def:
εὐ-αρέοτως 
adv., 
acceptably: τ, θεῷ, Hébreux 12:28.†

G2103.def:
Εὔβουλος, -ου, ὁ. 
Eubulus, a Christian: 2 Timothée 4:21.†

G2104.def:
εὐγενής, -ές
(εὖ, γένος), [in LXX: Job 1:3 (גָּדוֹל), 2Ma.10:13 R, 4Ma.6:5 4Mac 9:13 4Mac 9:23 4Mac 9:27 4Mac 10:3 4Mac 10:15 * ;] 
__1. well born, of noble race: Luc 19:12, 1 Corinthiens 1:26. 
__2. noble-minded: compar., -έστερος, Actes 17:11.†

G2105.def:
εὐδία, -ας, ἡ 
(εὔδιος, calm) [in LXX: Sir.3:15 * ;] 
fair weather: Matthieu 16:2 (Rec., R, txt.).†

G2107.def:
εὐδοκία, -ας, ἡ
(εὐδοκέω, which see), [in LXX: Psaumes 5:12, al. (רָצוֹן), frequently in Sir; in Inscr. (I.G., 5960), LXX, and NT = εὐδόκησις (Died.) ;] 
good pleasure, good-will, satisfaction, approval: Matthieu 11:26, Luc 10:21, Romains 10:1, Éphésiens 1:5, 9, Philippiens 1:15 2:13; with genitive obj., 2 Thessaloniciens 1:11 (see Milligan, in l); ἐν ἀνθρώποις εὐδοκία, Rec., R, mg., WH, mg. (see Field, Notes, 48 f.), Luc 2:14; -ας, Lk, l.with, R, txt., WH, txt. (see ICC, in l; WH, App., in l).†

G2108.def:
εὐεργεσία, -ας, ἡ
(εὐεργέτης), [in LXX: Psaumes 78:11 (עֲלִילָה), Wis.16:11, 24, 2Ma.6:13 2Mac 9:26, 4Ma.8:17 * ;] 
a good deed, kindness, benefit: 1 Timothée 6:2; with genitive of person(s) (εὐ. πόλεως, Plat., leg., 805b), Actes 4:9,†

G2109.def:
εὐεργετέω, -ῶ
(εὐεργέτης), [in LXX: Psaumes 13:6 (גָּמַל), Wis.3:5, al. ;] 
to do good, bestow benefit: Actes 10:33.†

G2110.def:
εὐεργέτης, -ου, ὁ 
[in LXX: Esther 8:13, Wis.19:14, 2Ma.4:2, 3Ma.3:19 3Mac 6:24 * ;] 
a benefactor: Luc 22:25 (for contemp. usage, see Deiss., LAE, 248).†

G2111.def:
εὔ-θετος, -ον
(τίθημι), [in LXX: Psaumes 32:6 (מָצָא), From Th Sus 1:15* ;] 
ready for use, fit: of things, with dative, Hébreux 6:7; before εἰς, Luc 14:35; of persons, with dative, Luc 9:62 (for rabbinic parallels, see Dalman, Words, 119 f.).†

G2112.def:
εὐθέως 
adv. (εὐθύς), [in LXX: Job 5:3 (פִּתְאוֹם), Wis.5:12, 1Ma.11:12, al. ;] 
straightway, at once, directly: Galates 1:16, Jacques 1:24, 3Jn.14 (cf. Dalman, Words, 28 f.), Apocalypse 4:2, and frequently in Mt, Lk, Jo, Ac (in Mk, εὐθύς), which see)

G2113.def:
εὐθυδρομέω, -ῶ 
of ships, to run a straight course (Philo): Actes 16:11 21:1.†

G2114.def:
εὐθυμέω, -ῶ
(ὔθυμος), [in Sm.: Psaumes 32:11, Proverbes 15:15 * ;] 
__1. trans., to make cheerful (Æsch.). 
__2. Intrans. (Eur., Plut.; so mid. in Xen., Plat.), to be of good cheer: Actes 27:22, 25, Jacques 5:13.†

G2115.def:
εὔ-θυμος, -ον 
[in LXX: 2Ma.11:26 * ;] 
__1. kind (Hom.). 
__2. of good cheer (Æsch., al.): Actes 27:36.†

G2116.def:
εὐθύνω
(εὐθύς), [in LXX: Nombres 22:23, Josué 24:23 (נָטָה hi.), Juges 14:7, 1 Rois 18:20 18:26 (יָשַׁר) Proverbes 20:24, Sir.2:2, 6, al. ;] 
__1. to direct: Jacques 3:4. 
__2. to make straight: Jean 1:23 (LXX, ἑτοιμάσατε).†

G2117.def:
εὐθύς, -εῖα, -ύ 
[in LXX chiefly for יָשַׁר ;] 
__1. straight, direct: τρίβοι, Matthieu 3:3, Marc 1:3, Luc 3:4" (LXX) ; εἰς εὐθειας, (sc. ὁδούς), Luc 3:5; εὐ. ὐδός, figuratively, Actes 13:10, 2 Pierre 2:15; as (Proper name) of a street, Actes 9:11. 
__2. In moral sense, straightforward, right: καρδία, Actes 8:21 (cf. Psaumes 7:11 32:11, al.).†
εὐθύς, 
adv., [in LXX (more frequently than εὐθέως) chiefly for יָשַׁר ;] 
= εὐθέως, straightway, directly: Matthieu 3:16 13:20-21 14:27 21:2-3 26:74, Luc 6:49, Jean 13:30, 32 19:34, Actes 10:16, 42 times in Mk.†

G2118.def:
εὐθύτης, -ητος, ἡ
(εὐθύς), [in LXX chiefly for יֹשֶׁר, מִישׁוֹר and cognate forms ;] 
uprightness: Hébreux 1:8 (LXX).†

G2119.def:
εὐκαιρέω, -ῶ
(= cl., εὖ σχολῆς ἔχειν; used by Polyb. and Philo; cf. Rutherford, NPhr. 205; MM, Exp., xiv), 
to have leisure or opportunity: 1 Corinthiens 16:12; with inf., Marc 6:31; before εἰς, to devote one's leisure to, Actes 17:21.†

G2120.def:
εὐκαιρία, -ας, ἡ
(εὔκαιρος), [in LXX: Psaumes 9:10 (see Soph., Lex., see word) Psaumes 10:1 145:15 (עֵת), Sir.38:24, 1Ma.11:42 * ;] 
fitting time, opportunity: before ἵνα, Matthieu 26:16; τοῦ, with inf., Luc 22:6.†

G2121.def:
εὔ-καιρος, -ον 
[in LXX: Psaumes 104:27 (עֵת), 2Ma.14:29 2Mac 15:20-21, 3Ma.4:11 3Mac 5:44 * ;] 
timely, seasonable, suitable (Cremer, 740): ἡμέρα, Marc 6:21 (or empty, as in Byz. and MGr.; see MM, Exp., xiv); βοήθεια, Hébreux 4:16.†

G2122.def:
εὐκαίρως 
adv., [in LXX: Sir.18:22 * ;] 
seasonably, in season: Marc 14:11; opposite to ἀκ- (Kühner3, iv, 346 d), 2 Timothée 4:2.†

G2123.def:
εὔ-κοπος, -ον 
[in LXX: Sir.22:15, 1Ma.3:18 * ;] 
with easy labour, easy: compar., -ώτερόν ἐστι, with inf., Matthieu 9:5, Marc 2:9, Luc 5:23; with accusative and inf., Matthieu 19:24, Marc 10:25, Luc 16:17 18:25 (Polyb.; the adv. -ως occurs in Aristoph., Fr., 615).†

G2124.def:
εὐλάβεια, -ας, ἡ
(εὐλαβής), [in LXX: Jérémie 22:24 (דְּאָגָה), Proverbes 28:14, Wis.17:8 * ;] 
__1. caution, discretion (Soph., Plat., al.). 
__2. In later Gk. (Diod., Plut., al.), also reverence, godly fear: Hébreux 5:7 12:28.†

G2125.def:
εὐλαβέομαι, -οῦμαι 
[in LXX: Proverbes 30:5, Nahum 1:7 (חָסָה), al., for 15 different Heb. words in all; also Sir.7:29 41:3, al. ;] 
__1. to be cautious, to beware: Actes 23:10 (Rec.; φοβηθείς, WH, RV). 
__2. to reverence: Hébreux 11:7 (cf. Cremer, 388).†

G2126.def:
εὐλαβής, -ές
(εὖ, λαβεῖν), [in LXX: Michée 7:2 AB2 (חָסִיד); εὐ. ποιεῖν, Lévitique 15:31 (נָזַר hi.), Sir.11:7 א2* ;] 
__1. cautious, circumspect. 
__2. devout, religious, reverent: Actes 2:5 8:2 22:12; δίκαιος καὶ εὐ., Luc 2:25.†

G2127.def:
εὐλογέω, -ῶ 
[in LXX chiefly for בָּרַךְ pi. ;] 
__1. to speak well of, praise (cl.; LXX Deutéronome 8:10, al.): τ. θεόν, Luc 1:64 2:28 24:51, 53 (αἰνοῦντες, T, WH, mg.), Jacques 3:9; absol., to give praise, Matthieu 14:19 26:26 (see Swete on Marc 14:22), Marc 6:41 14:22 (see Swete, in l), Luc 24:30, 1 Corinthiens 14:16. 
__2. As in LXX (= בָּרַךְ pi.); 
__(a) to bless, invoke blessings on (Genèse 24:60, Nombres 23:20, al.): absol., 1 Corinthiens 4:12, 1 Pierre 3:9; with accusative of person(s), Luc 2:34 6:28 24:50-51, Romains 12:14, Hébreux 7:1, 6-7 11:20-21; εὐλογημένος (= בָּרַךְ; see Lft., Notes, 310; DCG, i, 189), blessed, Matthieu 21:9 23:39" (LXX), Marc 11:9-10, Luc 13:35 19:38" (LXX), Jean 12:13; with accusative of thing(s), Marc 8:7, Luc 9:16, 1 Corinthiens 10:16; 
__(b) with God as subject (Psaumes 44:3, al.), to bless, prosper, bestow blessings on: with accusative of person(s), Actes 3:26, Galates 3:9, Éphésiens 1:3 (Lft., Notes, 311), Hébreux 6:14; εὐλογημένος, Luc 1:28 (WH, tit., R, tit., omit) Luc 1:42; εὐλογημένοι τ. πατρός (cf. Ésaïe 61:9), Matthieu 25:34; pass. Actes 3:25 (cf. ἐν-, κατ-ευλογέω).†
SYN.: see: αἰνέω, and cf. DCG, i, 189, 211; Cremer, 766

G2129.def:
εὐλογία, -ας, ἡ
[in LXX chiefly for בְּרָכָה ;] 
__1. fair speaking, flattering speech: χρηστολογίας καὶ εὐ., Romains 16:18. 
__2. praise: of God (as in late Inscr.; LS, see word) and Christ, Apocalypse 5:12-13 7:12 
__3. In LXX and NT: blessing, benediction; 
__(a) the act of blessing: 1 Corinthiens 10:16, Hébreux 12:17, Jacques 3:10; 
__(b) concrete, a blessing: Romains 15:29, 2 Corinthiens 9:5-6, Galates 3:14, Éphésiens 1:3, Hébreux 6:7, 1 Pierre 3:9 (cf. Deutéronome 11:26, Sir.7:32, al.).†

G2130.def:
εὐ-μετά-δοτος, -ον
(εὖ, μεταδιδωμι), 
ready to impart: assoc. with κοινωνικός (for the distinction between the two, see Field, Notes, 213; CGT, in l), 1 Timothée 6:18.†

G2132.def:
εὐ-νοέω, -ῶ
(εὔνοος, friendly), [in LXX: Esther 8:13 Bא1, Dan LXX 2:43, 3Ma.7:11 * ;] 
to be favourable, kindly disposed: with dative, Matthieu 5:25.†

G2133.def:
εὔνοια, -ας, ἡ
(εὔνοος), [in LXX: Esther 2:23, al. ;] 
goodwill: Éphésiens 6:7 (of slaves; cf. MM, Exp., xiv).†

G2134.def:
εὐνουχίζω
(εὐνοῦχος), 
to make a eunuch of, castrate: pass., Matthieu 19:12; metaphorically, εὐ. έαυτόν, ib.†

G2135.def:
εὐνοῦχος, -ου, ὁ
(i.e. ὁ τὴν εὐνὴν(bed) ἔχων), [in LXX for סָרִיס (perhaps not of necessity an actual eunuch; DB, see word), Genèse 39:1, al., Wis.3:14, Sir.20:4 30:20 ;] 
an emasculated man, a eunuch: Matthieu 19:12; one such holding, as was common, high office, as of chamberlain, at court, Actes 8:27, 34-39; metaphorically, of one naturally incapacitated for or volun­tarily abstaining from wedlock, Matthieu 19:12.†

G2136.def:
Εὐοδία (Rec. -ωδία), -ας, ἡ 
Euodia (not as AV, Euodias), a Christian woman: Philippiens 4:2.†

G2137.def:
εὐ-οδόω, -ῶ
(ὁδός), [in LXX chiefly for צָלַח hi. ;] 
to help on one's way (Soph., al.). Pass., to have a prosperous journey; metaphorically (Hdt., al.), to prosper, be prospered, be successful: 3Jn.2, Romains 1:10, 1 Corinthiens 16:2 (on the tense, see M, Pr., 54; ICC, in l).†

G2138.def:
εὐ-πειθής, ές,
(εὖ, πείθομαι), [in LXX: 4Ma.12:6 AR* ;] 
ready to obey, compliant: Jacques 3:17.†

G2139.def:
εὐ-περί-στατος, -ον
(εὖ, περιΐστημι), 
of sins, readily besetting: Hébreux 12:1 (on form and sense of the word, see Westc., in l).†

G2140.def:
εὐ-ποιία (Rec. -ιΐα), -ας, ἡ 
__1. beneficence, doing good: Hébreux 13:16. 
__2. a benefit (FlJ, Ant., ii, ll, 2, al.).†

G2141.def:
εὐ-πορέω, -ῶ
(εὔτορος, well provided for) [in LXX: Lévitique 25:26, 49 נָשַׂג hi.), Lévitique 25:23 (seel.), Wis.10:10 * ;] 
to prosper, be well off: Actes 11:29.†

G2142.def:
εὐ-πορία, -ας, ἡ
(εὔπορος), [in LXX for חַיִל, 4Ki.25:10 A (frequently in Aq.)* ;] 
__1. facility. 
__2. plenty, wealth: Actes 19:25.†

G2143.def:
εὐ-πρέπεια, -ας, ἡ
(εὐπρεπής, comely), [in LXX for הָדָר, etc. ;] 
goodly appearance, comeliness: Jacques 1:11.†

G2144.def:
εὐ-πρόσ-δεκτος, -ον
(εὖ, προσδέχομαι) 
more usual than δέκτος, which see, acceptable: Romains 15:16, 31, 2 Corinthiens 6:2 8:12, 1 Pierre 2:5.†

G2145.def:
εὐ-πρόσ-εδρος, -ον 
Rec. for εὐπάρεδρος, which see: 1 Corinthiens 7:35.†

G2146.def:
εὐ-προσωπέω, -ῶ
(εὐπρόσωπος, fair of face), [in Al.: Psaumes 141:6, seel. for -ίζω* ;] 
to look well, make a fair show: metaphorically (as in 7.; see Deiss., LAE, 96), Galates 6:12.†

G2147.def:
εὑρίσκω, 
[in LXX chiefly for מצא, also for נשׂג hi., etc. ;] 
to find, with or without previous search: absol., opposite to ζητέω, Matthieu 7:7, 8 Luc 11:9, 10; with accusative, Matthieu 2:8, Marc 1:37, Actes 13:22, 2 Timothée 1:17, al.; pass., οὐχ εὑ., of disappearance, Hébreux 11:5, Apocalypse 16:20, al.; γῆ κ. τὰ ἐν αὐτῇ ἔργα εὑρεθήσεται (for conjectures as to the meaning of this reading, see Mayor, ICC, in l.), 2 Pierre 3:10, WH, R, mg. Metaphorical, to find, find out by inquiry, learn, discover: Luc 19:48, Actes 4:21; αἰτίαν, Jean 18:38, Actes 13:28, al.; pass., Matthieu 1:18, Luc 17:18, Romains 7:10, 1 Corinthiens 4:2, Galates 2:17, 1 Pierre 1:7, Apocalypse 5:4, al.; of attaining to the knowledge of God, εὑ. θεόν, Actes 17:27; pass., Romains 10:20 (LXX). Mid., to find for oneself, gain, procure, obtain: with accusative of thing(s), λύτρωσιν, Hébreux 9:12; act. in same sense (so cl. poets, but not in Attic prose), Matthieu 10:39 11:29, Luc 1:30, Actes 7:46, 2 Timothée 1:18, al. (cf. ἀν-ευρίσκω).

G2148.def:
Εὐρ-ακύλων (Rec. εὐροκλύδων, which see), -ωνος 
(Εὖρος, the East wind, and Lat. Aquilo; Vg., Euroaquilo), 
the Euraquilo, a N.E. wind (i.e. between Eurus and Aquilo): Actes 27:14.†
εὐρο-κλύδων (G, εὐροκλ-), -ωνος, ὁ 
(Εὖρος (seel. εὐρύς, broad), κλύδων), 
Euroclydon (prob. a sailor's corruption of Εὐρακύλων, which see): Actes 17:14, Rec,†

G2149.def:
εὐρύ-χωρος, -ον 
(εὐρύς, broad + χώρα), [in LXX for רָחַב ni., and cognate forms (Ésaïe 30:23, al.), exc. 2 Chroniques 18:9 (גֹּרֶן ;) 
spacious, broad: Matthieu 7:13.†

G2150.def:
εὐ-σέβεια, -ας, ἡ
(εὐσεβής, which see), [in LXX: Proverbes 1:7, Ésaïe 33:6 (יִרְאָה), Proverbes 13:11 (aliter in Heb.), Ésaïe 11:2 (יְהוָֹה יִרְאָה), I Esther 1:23, Wis.10:12, Sir.49:3, and very frequently in 4Mac ;] 
__1. piety, reverence (towards parents and others). 
__2. piety towards God, godliness: Actes 3:12, 1 Timothée 2:2 4:7-8 6:5-6 6:11, 2 Pierre 1:3 1:6-7; τὸ τῆς εὐ. μυστήριον, 1 Timothée 3:16; ἡ κατ᾽ εὐ. διδασκαλία, 1 Timothée 6:3; ἡ ἀλήθεια ἡ κατ᾽ εὐ., Tite 1:1; μόρφωσις εὐσεβείας, 2 Timothée 3:5; pl. (see Bl., § 32, 6; Mayor on Jacques 2:1), 2 Pierre 3:11 (on the use of εὐ. and cognates in Past. Epp., see CGT, on 1 Timothée 2:2; cf. also Cremer, 524).†

G2151.def:
εὐ-σεβέω, -ῶ
(εὐσεβής, which see), [in LXX: Dan LXX Sus 1:64, 4Ma.9:6 אR, 4Ma.11:5 4Mac 11:8 4Mac 11:23 4Mac 18:2 * ;] 
to reverence, show piety towards; with accusative (else­where more frequently before εἰς., περί, πρός): οἶκον, 1 Timothée 5:4; θεόν, Actes 17:23 (Cremer, 525).†

G2152.def:
εὐσεβής, -ές
(εὖ, σέβομαι), [in LXX: Proverbes 12:12, Ésaïe 24:16 26:7 (צַדִּיק), Michée 7:2 (חָסִיד), Ésaïe 32:8 (נָדִיב), and frequently in Sirach and 4Maccabees ;] 
pious, godly, devout: Actes 10:2, 7, 2 Pierre 2:9.†
SYN.: θεοσεβής, θρῆσκος (see Tr., Syn., § xlviii; DB, ii, 221 f.; Cremer, 524 f., 858)

G2153.def:
εὐσεβῶς 
adv., [in LXX: 4Ma.7:21 * ;] 
piously, religiously: 2 Timothée 3:12, Tite 2:12.†

G2154.def:
εὔσημος, -ον
(εὖ + οῆμα, a sign) [in LXX for כֶּסֶא, Psaumes 81:3 (-ως, from LXX 219)* ;] 
__1. conspicuous (cf. Ps, l.with). 
__2. clear to the understanding, distinct: 1 Corinthiens 14:9.†

G2155.def:
εὔσπλαγχνος, -ον
(εὖ, σπλάγχνον, which see), [in Man.1.7 (Camb. Manual LXX, iii, 825) ;] 
__1. in Hippocr., as medical term (LS, see word). 
__2. Metaphorical (cf. εὐσιλαγχνία, Eurip., Rhes., 192), in NT, tenderhearted, compassionate: Éphésiens 4:32, 1 Pierre 3:8.†

G2156.def:
εὐσχημόνως 
adv. (εὐσχήμων), 
decorously, becomingly: 1 Corinthiens 14:40; περιπατεῖν, Romains 13:13, 1 Thessaloniciens 4:12.†

G2158.def:
εὐσχήμωι, -ον
(εὖ, σχῆμα), [in LXX: Proverbes 11:25 * ;] 
__1. elegant, graceful, comely (Eur., Plat., al.): τὰ εὐ. ἡμῶν (opposite to τὰ ἀσχ- ἡμ-), 1 Corinthiens 12:24; in moral sense, seemly, becoming, 1 Corinthiens 7:35. 
__2. Also in late Gk. (see Swete, Mk., l.with; MM, Exp., xiv), wealthy, influential (RV, of honourable estate): Marc 15:43, Actes 13:50 17:12.†

G2159.def:
εὐτόνως 
adv. (εὖ, τείνω), [in LXX forשׁוֹפָר Josué 6:8 * ;] 
vigorously, vehemently: Luc 23:10, Actes 18:28.†

G2160.def:
εὐτραπελία, -ας, ἡ
(εὖ, τρέπω), 
__1. versatility, wit, facetiousness (Hippocr., Plat., al.). 
__2. = βωμολογία, coarse jesting, ribaldry (Abbott, Essays, 93): Éphésiens 5:4.†
SYN.: μωρολογία, see Tr., Syn., § xxxiv

G2161.def:
Εὔτυχος, -ου, ὁ
(εὖ, τυχή), 
Butychus, a young man: Actes 20:9.†

G2162.def:
εὐφημία, -ας, ἡ
(εὔφημος), [in Sm.: Psaumes 42:5 47:2 100:2 126:2 * ;] 
good report, praise: opposite to δυσφημία, 2 Corinthiens 6:8.†

G2163.def:
εὔφημος, -ον
(εὖ, φήμη), [in Sm.: Psaumes 63:6 ;] 
primarily, utter­ing words or sounds of good omen, hence, 
__1. avoiding ill-omened words, religiously silent. 
__2. fair-sounding, auspicious (R, mg., gracious): Philippiens 4:8.†

G2165.def:
εὐφραίνω 
[in LXX chiefly for שָׂמַח, qal, pi. ;] 
to cheer, gladden: with accusative of person(s), opposite to λυπεῖν, 2 Corinthiens 2:2. Pass., to be happy, rejoice, make merry: Luc 15:32, Actes 2:26" (LXX) Romains 15:10 (LXX), Galates 4:27 (LXX), Apocalypse 11:10 12:12; before ἐν, Actes 7:41; ἐπί with dative, Apocalypse 18:20; of merry-making at a feast (3Ki.4:20; of. Kennedy, Sources, 155; Field, Notes, 69 f.), Luc 12:19 15:23-24, 29" (LXX) (λαμπρῶς) Luc 16:19.†

G2166.def:
Εὐφράτης, -ου, ὁ 
the river Euphrates: Apocalypse 9:14 16:12.†

G2167.def:
εὐφροσύνη, -ης, ἡ
(εὔφρων, cheerful) [in LXX chiefly for שִׂמְחָה ;] 
rejoicing, gladness: Actes 2:28 (LXX) Actes 14:17.†

G2168.def:
εὐχαριστέω, -ῶ 
[in LXX: Jdth.8:25 Wis.18:2, 2Ma.1:11 2Mac 10:7 A 2Ma.12:31 R, 3Ma.7:16 * ;] 
to be thankful, give thanks (chiefly in late writers and Inscr.; cf. Milligan, Th., 5; Ellic. on Colossiens 1:12; Lft., Notes, 9): Romains 1:21, 1 Corinthiens 14:17, 1 Thessaloniciens 5:18; of giving thanks before meat, Matthieu 15:36 26:27, Marc 8:6 14:23, Luc 22:17, 19, Jean 6:11, 23, 1 Corinthiens 11:24; with dative pens., τ. θεῷ, Luc 17:16, Actes 27:35 28:15, Romains 14:6 16:4, 1 Corinthiens 14:18, Philippiens 1:3, Colossiens 1:3, 12, Phm 4; before διὰ Ἰ. Χριστοῦ, Romains 1:8 7:25 R, WH, mg., Colossiens 3:17; ἐν ὀνόματι Χρ., Éphésiens 5:20; before περί, 1 Thessaloniciens 1:2, 2 Thessaloniciens 1:3; ὅτι, Romains 1:8, 2 Thessaloniciens 2:13; ἐπι, with dative of thing(s), 1 Corinthiens 1:4; ὐπέρ, 1 Corinthiens 10:30, Éphésiens 1:16 5:20; ὅτι, Luc 18:11, Jean 11:41, 1 Corinthiens 1:14, 1 Thessaloniciens 2:13, Apocalypse 11:17; pass. (Deiss., BS, 122 f.), 2 Corinthiens 1:11.†
SYN.: see: αἰνέω; and cf. Cremer, 903 f

G2169.def:
εὐχαριστία, -ας, ἡ
(εὐχάριστος), [in LXX: Esther 8:13, Wis.16:28, Sir.37:11, 2Ma.2:27 * ;] 
__1. thankfulness, gratitude (Polyb.; Es, Sir, 2Mac, ll. with): Actes 24:3. 
__2. giving of thanks, thanksgiving (so in π. and Inscr.; M, Th., 41 f.): 1 Corinthiens 14:16, 2 Corinthiens 4:15, Éphésiens 5:4, Philippiens 4:6, Colossiens 2:7 4:2, 1 Thessaloniciens 3:9, 1 Timothée 4:3-4, Apocalypse 4:9 7:12; with dative of person(s), 2 Corinthiens 9:11 (cf. τ. θεοῦ, Wis, l.with); pl., 2 Corinthiens 9:12, 1 Timothée 2:1 (Cremer, 904).†

G2170.def:
εὐχάριστος, -ον
(εὖ, χαρίζομαι), [in LXX for חֵן, Proverbes 11:16 * ;] 
__1. = εὔχαρις, winning, gracious, agreeable (Pr, l.with). 
__2. grateful, thankful: Colossiens 3:15.†

G2171.def:
εὐχή, -ῆς, ἡ
(εὔχομαι), [in LXX chiefly for נָדַר ;] 
__1. a prayer: Jacques 5:15. 
__2. a vow: Actes 18:18 21:23.†
SYN.: see: δέησις

G2172.def:
εὔχομαι 
[in LXX chiefly for נָדַד, also for עָתַר hi., etc. ;] 
to pray: with accusative of thing(s), 2 Corinthiens 13:9; with dative of person(s), τ. θεῷ, Actes 26:29; before πρὸς τ. θεόν, 2 Corinthiens 13:7; with accusative and inf., Actes 27:29, 3Jn.2; before ὑπέρ, Jacques 5:16; ηὐχόμην εἶναι (On imperfect here, see ICC, in l, Lft., Phm 13), Romains 9:3 (Cremer, 718).†

G2173.def:
εὔ-χρηστος, -ον
(εὖ, χράομαι), [in LXX: Proverbes 31:13 (חֵפֶץ), Wis.13:13 * ;] 
useful, serviceable: with dative of person(s), 2 Timothée 2:21; id. before εἰς, with dative of thing(s), 2 Timothée 4:11; opposite to ἄχρηστος, Phm 11.†

G2174.def:
εὐψυχέω, -ῶ
(εὔψυχος, courageous), 
to be of good courage: Philippiens 2:19.†

G2175.def:
εὐωδία, -ας, ἡ
(εὐώδης, fragrant; ὄζω) [in LXX for נִיחוֹחַ, Genèse 8:21, al. (ὀσμὴ εὐωδίας); Sir.20:9 24:15, al. ;] 
fragrance: metaphorically, Χριστοῦ εὐ,., 2 Corinthiens 2:15; ὀσμὴ εὐωδίας (a metaphor of sacrifice, most frequently in Pent. and Ez.), Éphésiens 5:2, Philippiens 4:18.†

G2176.def:
εὐώνυμος, -ον
(εὖ, ὄνομα), [in LXX chiefly for שְׂמֹאול ;] 
__1. of good name or omen. 
__2. Euphemistic for ἀριστερός, left: Actes 21:3, Apocalypse 10:2; ἐξ εὐωνύμων, on the left: Matthieu 20:21, 23 25:33, 41 27:38, Marc 10:40 15:27.†

G2177.def:
ἐφάλλομαι 
[in LXX for צָלַח, 1 Rois 10:6 11:6 16:13 * ;] 
to leap upon: before ἐπί with accusative of person(s) Actes 19:16.†

G2178.def:
ἐφ-άπαξ, 
adv. 
__1. once for all (Eupol.): Romains 6:10 Hébreux 7:27 9:12 10:10. 
__2. at once: 1 Corinthiens 15:6.†

G2181.def:
Ἔφεσος, -ου, ἡ 
Ephesus, a city in Asia Minor Actes 18:19, 21 18:24, 27 19:1, 17 19:26 (on the genitive, see M, Pr., 73) Actes 20:16-17, 1 Corinthiens 15:32 16:8, Éphésiens 1:1, 1 Timothée 1:3, 2 Timothée 1:18 4:12, Apocalypse 1:11 2:1.†

G2182.def:
ἐφ-ευρετής, -οῦ, ὁ
(ἐφευρίσκω, to find out) 
an inventor, contriver: κακῶν (cf. κακίας εὑρετής, 2Ma.7:31), Romains 1:30.†

G2183.def:
ἐφ-ημερία, -ας, ἡ
(ἐφήμερος), [in LXX chiefly for מִשְׁמֶרֶת, מַחֲלֹקֶת ;] 
__1. a course of daily services (Néhémie 13:30, 1 Chroniques 25:8, al.). 
__2. a class or course of priests detailed for service in the temple (1 Chroniques 23:6, al.): Luc 1:5, 8 (cf. MGr., ἐφημέριος, priest).†

G2184.def:
ἐφ-ήμερος, -ον
(ἐπί, ἡμέρα), 
__1. lasting for a day. 
__2. daily, for the day: Jacques 2:15.†

G2185.def:
ἐφ-ικνέομαι, -οῦμαι 
[in LXX: Sir.43:27, 30 R (ἀφικ- ABא)* ;] 
to come to, to reach: before ἄχρι, 2 Corinthiens 10:13; εἰς, 2 Corinthiens 10:14.†

G2187.def:
Ἐφραίμ, (-ΐμ, Tr.) 
Ephraim, a town near Jerusalem: Jean 11:54.†

G2188.def:
ἐφφαθά (Aram. אֶתְפְּתח, see Abbott, Essays, 142 ff.; DCG, i, 522) 
ephphatha, be opened: Marc 7:34.†

G2189.def:
ἔχθρα, -ας, ἡ
(ἐχθρός), [in LXX for אֵיבָה, שִׂנְאָה, etc. ;] 
enmity: Luc 23:12, Romains 8:7, Galates 5:20, Éphésiens 2:15-16, Jacques 4:4.†
ἀηδία, -ας, ἡ 
(ἀ- neg., ἦδος, pleasure), [in LXX: Proverbes 23:29 (שִׂיחַ)* ;] 
__1. of things or persons, unpleasantness, odiousness (Hipp., Dem., al.) 
__2. dislike (Plat.). disagreement (MM, VGT, see word): Luc 23:12 D.†

G2190.def:
ἐχθρός, -ά, -όν
(ἔχθος, hatred), [in LXX chiefly for אֵיבָה, also for עָר, etc. ;] 
__1. hated, hateful (Hom.): opposite to ἀγαπητός, Romains 11:28. 
__2. Actively, hating, hostile: Romains 5:10, 1 Corinthiens 15:25, 2 Thessaloniciens 3:15; with genitive of person(s) (cl.), Jacques 4:4; τ. διανοίᾳ, Colossiens 1:21; ἐ. ἄνθρωπος, Matthieu 13:28; as subst., ὁ ἐ., an enemy, 1 Corinthiens 15:26; the devil, Matthieu 13:39, Luc 10:19; with genitive of person(s), Matthieu 22:44 Marc 12:36, Luc 20:43, Actes 2:35, 1 Corinthiens 15:25, Hébreux 1:13 10:13" (LXX) ; Matthieu 5:43-44 10:36 13:25, Luc 1:71, 74 6:27, 35 19:27, 43, Romains 12:20, Galates 4:16, Apocalypse 11:5, 12; with genitive of thing(s), Actes 13:10, Philippiens 3:18.†

G2191.def:
ἔχιδνα, -ης, ἡ 
[in OT (Aq.), Ésaïe 59:5 * ;] 
a viper: Actes 28:3; metaphorically, γεννήματα ἐχιδνῶν, Matthieu 3:7 12:34 23:33, Luc 3:7.†

G2194.def:
Ζαβουλών, ὁ indecl. (Heb. זְבוּלוּן see Genèse 30:20) 
Zebulun, Jacob's tenth son: the tribe of Z., Matthieu 4:13, 15, Apocalypse 7:8.†

G2195.def:
Ζακχαῖος, -ου, ὁ (Heb. זַכַּי, cf. Néhémie 7:14, I Esther 2:9, LXX Ζακχού), 
Zaccai, Zacchaeus, a publican: Luc 19:2, 5 19:8 (cf. 2Ma.10:19).†

G2196.def:
Ζαρά, ὁ indecl. (Heb. זֶרַח, Genèse 38:30), 
Zerah, an ancestor of Jesus: Matthieu 1:3.†

G2198.def:
ζάω, -ῶ, 
[in LXX chiefly for חיה (most frequently ptcp., ζῶν, inf., ζῆν, for חַי ;] 
__1. prop., to live, be alive (see Syn., see word βίος; in cl. usually of animal life, but sometimes of plants, as Arist., Eth. N, i, 7, 12): Actes 20:12, Romains 7:1-3, 1 Corinthiens 7:39, Apocalypse 19:20, al.; ἐν αὐτῷ ζῶμεν, Actes 17:28; ἐμοὶ τὸ ζῆν Χριστός, Philippiens 1:21; διὰ παντὸς τοῦ ζῆν (M, Pr., 215, 249), Hébreux 2:15; ὃ δὲ νῦν ζῶ ἐν σαρκί, Galates 2:20; ζῇ ἐν ἐμοὶ Χριστός, Galates 2:20; (ὁ) ζῶν, of God (אֵל חַי and cognate phrases, Josué 3:10, Osée 2:1 (1:10), Ésaïe 37:4, al.; see DCG, ii, 39a), Matthieu 16:16, Jean 6:57, Romains 9:26, 1 Thessaloniciens 1:9, Hébreux 3:12, Apocalypse 7:2, al.; in juristic phrase, ζῶ ἐγώ (חַי־אָנִי, Nombres 14:21, al.), as I live, Romains 14:11; ζῆν ἐπ᾽ ἄρτῳ, Matthieu 4:4, al.; ἐκ, 1 Corinthiens 9:14; of coming to life, Mrk.16:[11], Romains 6:10 14:9, 2 Corinthiens 13:4; opposite to νεκρός, Apocalypse 1:18 2:8; metaphorically, Luc 15:32; ζῆν ἐκ νεκρῶν, Romains 6:13; of the spiritual life of Christians, Luc 10:28, Jean 5:25, Romains 1:17 8:13; εἰς τ. αἰῶνα, Jean 6:51, 58; σὺν Χριστῷ, 1 Thessaloniciens 5:10; ὄνομα ἔχεις ὅτι ζῇς, Apocalypse 3:1. 
__2. As sometimes in cl., = βιόω, to live, pass one's life: Luc 2:36, Actes 26:5, Romains 7:9, Colossiens 2:20; ἐν πίστει, Galates 2:20; ἐν τ. ἁμαρτίᾳ, Romains 6:2; εὐσεβῶς, 2 Timothée 3:12; ἀσώτως, Luc 15:13; with dative (cl.), ἑαυτῳ (Field, Notes, 164), Romains 14:7, 2 Corinthiens 5:15; τ. δικαιοσύνῃ, Luc 20:38, Romains 6:10, 11 Galates 2:19; τ. Χριστῷ, 2 Corinthiens 5:15; τ. θεῷ, 1 Pierre 2:24; πνεύματι, Galates 5:25; κατὰ σάρκα, Romains 8:12, 13; 
__3. Of inanimate things, metaphorically: ὕδωρ ζῶν (i.e. springing water, as opposite to still water), in a spiritual sense, Jean 4:10, 11 7:38 (DCG, ii, 39f.): ἐλπὶς ζῶσα, 1 Pierre 1:3; ὁδὸς ζῶσα, Hébreux 10:20 (cf. ἀνα-, συν-ζάω; Cremer, 270, 721).

G2199G.def:
Ζεβεδαῖος, -ου, ὁ (Heb. זְבַדְיָה; LXX: Ζαβδειά, Esther 8:8 10:20; Ζαβαδαῖας, I Esther 9:35; Ζαβαδαῖος, I Esther 9:21) 
Zebedee, father of James and John the Apostles: Matthieu 4:21 10:2 20:20 26:37 27:56, Marc 1:19-20 3:17 10:35, Luc 5:10, Jean 21:2.†
